target_times_caveat: CAVEAT: the 42-day / 6-week figure is the generic limit in THL Ohjaus 21/2016 §4.1 (referral arrival → first treatment), the reference the strategy names for Goal 3 (S p.5). Day-28 alert and the 80% target are Tasan design choices, not official targets.
tasan_clock_note: Target per THL Ohjaus 21/2016 (marked outdated; no lung-specific limit; new cancer-specific targets due 2026-28, roadmap 3.1.2). Day-28 alert and 80% goal are Tasan design choices.

target_reference.label: THL maximum time from referral arrival to first cancer treatment (all cancers; no lung-specific target exists)
target_reference.caveat: Clock starts at referral arrival. No public regional statistic reports compliance with this target. The PDF is watermarked 'Vanhentunut' (outdated), but the 2026-2035 strategy still cites it.

headlines.ci_method: Values and 95% CIs read off the report's chart (Kuva 16), +/-1 pp; not published as numbers
headlines.source_table: Keuhkosyöpä Suomessa 2019-2023 (Syöpärekisteri/FICAN, publ. 23.4.2026), Kuva 16 (age-standardised, by sex); crude: Taulukko 11
headlines.caveat: Chart estimate, age-adjusted, not stage-adjusted, not survival. Values read by Tasan from the report's age-standardised chart (Kuva 16, +/-1 percentage point), not published numbers. Lung cancers (C33-C34) diagnosed 2019-2023 among residents of each wellbeing county; share with surgery or curative radiotherapy recorded in national registers within 12 months of diagnosis. Not adjusted for stage (missing for 48% nationally), comorbidity or fitness, and depends on regional treatment recording. Confidence intervals do not overlap for either sex.

regions.name: Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county

crude_secondary.ci_method: Wilson 95% CI computed by Tasan from printed n/N (not printed in report)
crude_secondary.caveat: Crude share of all lung cancers (C33-C34) diagnosed 2019-2023 among residents of each wellbeing county who had surgery or curative radiotherapy recorded in national registers within 12 months of diagnosis. Not survival and not adjusted for stage (missing for 48% nationally), comorbidity or fitness. Depends on regional treatment recording. The report's age-standardised chart shows the same gap for men and women, so age structure alone does not explain it.

headlines.goal_link: Goal 3 indicator 3 (proxy: starts at diagnosis, not referral)
headlines.label: Median days from lung cancer diagnosis to surgery: North Finland 13.5 vs South Finland 46.0
headlines.n: not printed per area; nationally about 1 in 10 patients (N=1 627) had any surgery within 6 months (report text, PDF p.17)
headlines.source_table: Keuhkosyöpä Suomessa (Syöpärekisteri, 12/2024), Taulukko 4.1, PDF p.28 (printed p.27); national median from text p.27
headlines.caveat: Lung cancers diagnosed Jan 2018-Jun 2022, by collaborative area of residence (5 areas, not wellbeing counties). Median days from Cancer Registry diagnosis date to surgery, only among patients whose first treatment within 6 months was surgery (nationally about 1 in 10 patients had surgery). Not the official 6-week referral-to-treatment clock. In the North at least a quarter of these patients have surgery on the diagnosis date (lower quartile 0 days), so the low median partly reflects how diagnosis is dated. Radiotherapy and drug-therapy medians do not show this North-South pattern.

headlines.label: Share of all lung cancer patients whose first active treatment started within 2 months of diagnosis: West Finland 27.7% vs Inland Finland 38.7%
headlines.ci_method: approximate Wilson 95% CI computed by Tasan; denominator = area patient total from Taulukko 3.3
headlines.source_table: Keuhkosyöpä Suomessa (2024), Taulukko 4.5 PDF p.34 (derived: surgery + non-palliative radiotherapy + drug therapy first-event columns at month 2) and Taulukko 3.3 PDF p.18
headlines.caveat: DERIVED by Tasan. Covers all lung cancers diagnosed Jan 2018-Jun 2022 among residents of each collaborative area. Measure: the cumulative share whose first recorded event within 2 months of the registry diagnosis date was surgery, non-palliative radiotherapy or drug therapy. Starts at diagnosis, not referral. West Finland includes Varsinais-Suomi, where drug therapy is barely recorded in registers (about 1% age-standardised vs 25% nationally), so part of the gap is recording, not care.

headlines.label: Age-standardised 1-year relative survival from lung cancer: North Finland 40.1% vs Inland Finland 46.8%
headlines.caveat: Age-standardised 1-year relative survival of lung cancer patients followed in 2020-2022, by collaborative area of residence, both sexes. One-year survival only: the strategy's indicator is 5-year survival against the Sweden-Norway average, and no public regional 5-year lung survival exists. Not adjusted for stage.

headlines.goal_link: Data gap (sub-goal 3.2: 90% data coverage, S p.36)
headlines.label: Stage at diagnosis is missing for 47.7% of lung cancers
headlines.caveat: All lung cancers diagnosed in Finland 2019-2023 (N=14 873): share with no stage information (no TNM, stage, verbal description or registry extent code). By county it ranges from about 22% to about 68% (Tasan's digitisation of report Kuva 13, +/-1 pp). Because stage is missing, no regional comparison can be stage-adjusted.

excluded.sotkanet_6411: Not used. Sotkanet 6411 is the share of non-urgent primary-care physician visits with a wait over 7 days (all causes, not cancer). Avohilmo data gaps in Vantaa, Kerava and Helsinki make county values unreliable (Vantaa-Kerava 85.4% in 2025 is an artefact risk).
excluded.colorectal_screening: Goal 2 context only (strategy p.5), not a Goal 3 indicator.

people_number.statement_en: If every wellbeing county below the national average had reached the national curative-treatment share (27.0%), about 65 more lung cancer patients a year would have had a curative-treatment record, about 12 of them in Lapland.
people_number.statement_fi: Jos jokainen kansallisen keskiarvon alle jäävä hyvinvointialue olisi yltänyt parantavan hoidon valtakunnalliseen osuuteen (27,0 %), noin 65 keuhkosyöpäpotilasta enemmän vuodessa olisi saanut parantavan hoidon merkinnän, heistä noin 12 Lapissa.
people_number.method: For each of the 12 wellbeing counties with a crude curative share below the national 4009/14873 = 26.95%: gap = 0.2695 x patients - patients with curative treatment. Summed gap 324.6 over 5 diagnosis years (2019-2023) divided by 5 = 64.9/yr (Lapland 60.4/5 = 12.1/yr). Computed by Tasan; not a published figure.
people_number.source_table: Keuhkosyöpä Suomessa 2019-2023 (Syöpärekisteri/FICAN, publ. 23.4.2026), Taulukko 11 (counts by wellbeing county)
people_number.caveat: Illustrative arithmetic by Tasan, not a published estimate and not a causal claim. Uses crude shares (not age- or stage-adjusted; stage is missing for 48% of lung cancers), so some of the gap may reflect older or less fit patients, later stage, or differences in how treatment is recorded. Benchmark is the national average, not a clinical optimum. 'Curative treatment' = surgery or curative radiotherapy recorded in national registers within 12 months. Does not say how many lives would be saved.
people_number.safe_wording_en: About 65 more lung cancer patients a year would get curative treatment if every below-average county reached the national rate, based on Cancer Registry counts for 2019-2023 (illustrative, not adjusted for stage).
